sourcedFrom: SIG HEXIUM™ SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102777-01 REV06 (printed on the back cover) (2026 (©2026 SIG SAUER Inc.))
cleanIntro: The HEXIUM 556 INC is SIG Sauer's 5.56 rifle suppressor in Inconel, threaded straight onto the barrel on a HUB mount. SIG builds the 5.56 HEXIUM in titanium or Inconel, and says the Inconel cans suit short barreled rifles and aggressive firing schedules where added durability is wanted. The 5.56 models come with a HUB mount for a 13/16-in. wrench. SIG's book is plain about the inside: HEXIUM suppressors need no internal cleaning, and nothing past unscrewing the HUB tapered mount from the body is authorized. So nothing in this guide opens the can. The maintenance SIG publishes is the threads, the outside of the body and an inspection, at least every 500 cartridges. Changing the HUB tapered mount is a configuration job in SIG's book, not part of cleaning, and is not in this guide.

steps.title: ⛔ Host unloaded, chamber checked by eye AND by touch
steps.action: Before the can comes off, make the host rifle safe following its own manual: unloaded, and the chamber checked both visually and physically. SIG asks for this every time a HEXIUM is installed, tightened or removed.
steps.prose: This book covers the suppressor, not the rifle it is on. For unloading the host, SIG sends you to the host's own operator's manual.
steps.quote: ALWAYS ENSURE THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED AND CLEARED BY VISUALLY AND PHYSICALLY INSPECTING THE CHAMBER PRIOR TO INSTALLING, TIGHTENING, OR REMOVING A SUPPRESSOR.
steps.cite: SIG HEXIUM™ SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102777-01 REV06 (printed on the back cover) — 3.1 ATTACHING SUPPRESSOR, WARNING UNLOAD/CLEAR, p.16

steps.title: ⛔ Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: Do not put a hand on the suppressor until it has cooled. A can that has just been shot is hot enough to burn bare skin, and it looks no different from a cold one.
steps.prose: Wait it out. Nothing in this guide is urgent enough to justify a burn.
steps.quote: NEVER TOUCH SUPPRESSOR WHEN HOT. FAILURE TO COMPLY MAY RESULT IN SEVERE BURNS TO UNPROTECTED SKIN.
steps.cite: SIG HEXIUM™ SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102777-01 REV06 (printed on the back cover) — 4.0 REMOVING SUPPRESSOR FROM FIREARM, WARNING HOT SURFACE, p.22
steps.warn: Never touch the suppressor when hot. Failure to comply may result in severe burns to unprotected skin.

steps.title: Break it loose with the wrench on the HUB mount
steps.action: Put the right wrench on the HUB mount and turn the suppressor counter-clockwise until it is loose enough to turn by hand. On the 5.56 models that is a 13/16-in. wrench.
steps.prose: It went on torqued, so it will not start by hand. If it gets harder to break loose from one cleaning to the next, carbon is building up between the can and the muzzle, and SIG's answer is to clean the base more often.
steps.caution: AS CARBON BUILDS UP BETWEEN THE SUPPRESSOR AND THE MUZZLE, IT WILL BECOME PROGRESSIVELY MORE DIFFICULT TO REMOVE THE SUPPRESSOR.
steps.aside: 5.56 models come standard with HUB mounts for 13/16-in. wrenches.
steps.quote: Using an appropriate wrench, loosen the suppressor until it can be turned by hand.
steps.cite: SIG HEXIUM™ SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102777-01 REV06 (printed on the back cover) — 4.0 REMOVING SUPPRESSOR FROM FIREARM, step 1, p.22

steps.title: Unscrew it the rest of the way off the barrel
steps.action: Keep turning the suppressor counter-clockwise by hand until it comes off the barrel. Leave the barrel's own muzzle threads (and any taper cap) on the rifle.
steps.prose: Take it straight off the threads rather than levering it. The threads on the can and the muzzle are both things you will inspect in a moment.
steps.quote: Continue to unscrew the suppressor from the barrel until it can be removed.
steps.cite: SIG HEXIUM™ SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102777-01 REV06 (printed on the back cover) — 4.0 REMOVING SUPPRESSOR FROM FIREARM, step 2, p.22

steps.title: ⛔ That is as far as it goes: no internal cleaning, no further disassembly
steps.action: Nothing else comes apart for cleaning. SIG states that HEXIUM suppressors need no internal cleaning, and that taking the suppressor apart beyond unscrewing its HUB tapered mount is not authorized. Everything below is work on the outside of a closed can.
steps.prose: A can SIG does not want opened is not a can you have failed to open. If you suspect a baffle or end-cap strike, or find damage, it goes to SIG's customer service.
steps.aside: HEXIUM suppressors do not require any internal cleaning.
steps.quote: FURTHER DISASSEMBLY OF THE SUPPRESSOR IS NOT AUTHORIZED. FAILURE TO COMPLY MAY DAMAGE SUPPRESSOR.
steps.cite: SIG HEXIUM™ SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102777-01 REV06 (printed on the back cover) — 6.1 REMOVAL, CAUTION, p.26

steps.title: Clean the suppressor's threads: nylon brush, never steel
steps.action: Clean any residue buildup off the suppressor's threads. Use a nylon brush for carbon. A steel wire brush damages the Cerakote finish.
steps.prose: Clean threads are what let the can come off next time without a fight.
steps.quote: Clean the suppressor threads of any residue buildup.
steps.cite: SIG HEXIUM™ SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102777-01 REV06 (printed on the back cover) — 5.1 CLEANING, step 1, p.25
steps.warn: DO NOT USE A STEEL WIRE BRUSH AS IT CAN DAMAGE THE CERAKOTE FINISH OF THE SUPRESSOR. USE A NYLON BRUSH FOR REMOVING CARBON BUILDUP.

steps.title: Wipe the body with CLP, then wipe it dry
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the suppressor body with a rag moistened with CLP to take off any residue, then wipe the body dry.
steps.prose: This is a wipe, not a soak. SIG warns that solvents can harm the surface finish and against over-lubricating, and nothing goes inside the can.
steps.quote: Wipe the suppressor body with a rag moistened with CLP to remove any residue. Wipe the body dry.
steps.cite: SIG HEXIUM™ SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102777-01 REV06 (printed on the back cover) — 5.1 CLEANING, step 2, p.25

steps.title: Clean the rifle's muzzle threads DRY: solvent, no CLP, no lube
steps.action: Clean residue off the rifle's muzzle threads with a nylon brush and a dry cleaning solvent similar to the one SIG names (MIL-P-D-680). Do not put CLP or any other lubricant on the muzzle threads.
steps.prose: This is the one place SIG says no to CLP: the suppressor body gets a CLP wipe, but the muzzle threads get solvent only and go back on dry.
steps.quote: Clean any residue buildup from the rifle's muzzle threads with a nylon brush and a dry cleaning solvent similar to (MIL-P-D-680). Do not use CLP or any other lubricant on the muzzle threads.
steps.cite: SIG HEXIUM™ SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102777-01 REV06 (printed on the back cover) — 5.1 CLEANING, step 3, p.25

steps.title: Inspect: threads, body, and the HUB mount secure in the body
steps.action: Check the rifle's muzzle threads and the HUB mount threads for damage. Check the suppressor body for damage. Make sure the HUB mount is secure in the suppressor body.
steps.prose: If you suspect a baffle or end-cap strike, SIG also wants the end cap and the body checked for signs of it, and any damage or suspected damage goes to customer service for repair.
steps.aside: If there is damage or suspected damage contact customer service for repair.
steps.quote: Ensure the HUB mount (4) is secure in the suppressor body.
steps.cite: SIG HEXIUM™ SUPPRESSORS — OPERATOR'S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8102777-01 REV06 (printed on the back cover) — 5.2 INSPECTION, step 3, p.25

deepAbsentReason: SIG's HEXIUM book states that HEXIUM suppressors do not require any internal cleaning (5.1 CLEANING, printed p.25) and, after the HUB tapered mount is unscrewed from the body, that further disassembly of the suppressor is not authorized (6.1 REMOVAL, CAUTION, printed p.26). The book prints no procedure that opens the body: its maintenance is the threads, the outside of the body and an inspection (pp.24–25), which are in the routine lane above. A can with damage or a suspected baffle or end-cap strike goes to SIG: the book asks the owner to contact customer service for repair (1.9 BAFFLE STRIKE, printed p.12). This listing therefore has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: THREADS
tasks: Suppressor threads cleaned of residue buildup.
Rifle's muzzle threads cleaned with a nylon brush and a dry cleaning solvent.
Never CLP or any other lubricant on the muzzle threads.
⛔ Never a steel wire brush: it damages the Cerakote finish.

cleaning.name: SUPPRESSOR BODY
tasks: Body wiped with a rag moistened with CLP.
Do not over-lubricate; solvents can harm the surface finish.

cleaning.name: INSPECTION
tasks: Muzzle threads and HUB mount threads checked for damage.
HUB mount secure in the suppressor body.
Damage or a suspected baffle or end-cap strike: contact SIG customer service.

cleaning.name: LEAVE ALONE
tasks: ⛔ No internal cleaning and no further disassembly of the suppressor.
⛔ Nothing put into the can: no water, oil, grease, wire pulling gel, ablatives or any other liquid.
⛔ No altered, added or substituted parts.

reassembly: Host rifle unloaded, chamber checked by eye and by touch.
Threads of both the muzzle and the suppressor clean (the muzzle threads dry, no lubricant).
The HEXIUM seats on a barrel with a 90 degree shoulder. On a barrel with a tapered shoulder, a taper cap goes on first — never the suppressor on a tapered barrel without one.
Muzzle device clear of the baffles: measured from the HUB mount flange to the end of the device, less than 1.45 in. on 5.56. SIG recommends the HUB mount directly on the barrel.
Thread the suppressor clockwise onto the barrel by hand.
With a crow's foot wrench (13/16-in. on the 5.56 HUB mount) on a torque wrench handle, tighten to 25-27 ft-lbf, or to the rifle manufacturer's recommended torque value.
fncheck: With the host unloaded and the chamber checked: the suppressor is threaded on clockwise and torqued to 25-27 ft-lbf (or the rifle maker's value), on a 90 degree shoulder or a taper cap, and the muzzle device is short enough not to touch the baffles. During use, check now and then that it is still tight on the barrel. If it is dropped or struck, inspect it for damage and make sure it is properly aligned with the barrel before firing again. ⛔ Jacketed projectiles to SAAMI specification only: never non-jacketed, frangible, tracer, multi-projectile or shot cartridges. Never fire it with water, debris or anything else inside, never pour water or ablatives into it, and stop firing if it overheats.
